The New India Assurance Co.
Ltd.
Vs. Sandhya Mohanta & Ors.

With Cot 111 of 2018 Sandhya Mohanta & Ors.
Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.

Mr. Rajesh Singh ....for the appellant Mr. Saidur
Rahaman ........for the claimants

The instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and award dated 20th December, 2017 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claim Tribunal cum Addl.
Dist Judge, Fast Track Court, CoochBehar in MAC Case No. 76 of 2009.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claim Tribunal cum Addl.
Dist Judge, Fast Track Court, CoochBehar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The brief fact of the case is that one company, namely, M/s. Kalpataru Power Transmission Ltd.
(Construction Department) under West Bengal State Electricity Board has been conducted some APDRP (re-conductoring) revised allocated by SE & CM Jalpaiguri (D) circle vide necessary approvals within Dinhata Subdivision.

The M/s. Kalpataru Power 1425 from CoochBehar Truck Owners Association for carrying electric polls having eight meters long from Setai to Dinhata on condition that the said polls will be loaded and unloaded by their own labourers.
According to such condition, the said polls were carrying by the said truck with eight labourers for loading and unloading from the said post from Setai to Dinhata.

On 03.07.2006, when the said truck loaded with electric polls and eight labourers reached at village Bara Kaimari under Situlkuchi P.S. at about 9:00 to 10:25 p.m., at the time another vehicle which was coming from opposite direction, then the said truck was given opportunity to cross the said vehicle with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and as a result the driver of the alleged truck lost his control over it as such the said truck was capsized in the side of the road.

All on a sudden three labourers out of eight were jumped in another side and the rest five labourers including the victim along with the said ECC polls were fallen down in the other side and the said five labourers were sustained severe multiple injuries all over their persons by pressure of the said electric post and died on the spot instantly.
The legal heirs of one of the labour(victim) filed an application before the learned Tribunal under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act for getting compensation.
The claim case was contested by the insurance company as well as the owner of the offending vehicle by filing written statement.
The learned Tribunal after hearing the notice and after receiving the evidences as awarded a sum of Rs.4,25,000/- and directed the insurance company to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said award, the insurance company has preferred this instant appeal.
The claimants also preferred a cross appeal against the said award for enhancement of the award.

sentences.text: 1 Learned advocate Mr. Rajesh Singh, appearing on behalf of the insurance company submits that the award passed by the learned Tribunal is erroneous in law and the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

In support of his contention he submits that the insurance policy which was marked as Exhibit - 7 before the learned Tribunal shows that the policy in respect of the vehicle is marked as 'liability only'.
Mr. Singh submits that according to the provisions of Section 147 of MV Act, the limits of liability of the insurance company to indemnify the owner is limited in the act itself.
"Liability only" policy means the statutory liability of the insurance company to indemnify the owner."
He refers to Section 147, Sub-section (b)(i) of the Act.

He submits that the statutory policy covered against any liability which may incur by him in respect of death of or bodily injury to any person including the owner of the goods or his authorized representative carried in the motor vehicle.
He submits that the offending vehicle is a truck and it is a goods vehicle; the owner of the goods and the authorized representative of the owner carried in the said motor vehicle are covered.
The present victim is the labour of M/s. Kalpataru Power Transmission Ltd., so they are not actually covered by the policy of insurance company.
He submits that the learned Tribunal has committed error and directed the insurance company to pay the compensation.
In this case the owner has violated the terms of the policy, so the owner of the offending vehicle may be directed to pay the compensation.
In support of his contention he cited a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court passed in Sanjeev Kumar Samart vs. Natinal Insurance Company Ltd. And Ors.

entities.text: Sanjeev Kumar Samart vs. Natinal Insurance Company Ltd. And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "24 . It is worthy to note that Sub-clause (I) (c) refers to an employee who is being carried in the vehicle covered by the policy.
Such vehicle being a goods carriage, an employee has to be covered by the statutory policy.

On an apposite reading of Sections 147 and 167 the intendemnt of the Legislature, as it appears to us, is to cover the injury to any person including the owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in a vehicle and an employee who is carried in the said vehicle.
It is apt to state here that the proviso commences in a different way.
A policy is not required to cover the liability of the employee except an employee covered under the 1923 Act and that too in respect of an employee carried in a vehicle.
To put it differently, it does not cover all kinds of employees.

Thus, on a contextual reading of the provision, schematic analysis of the Act and the 1923 Act, it is quite limpid that the statutory policy only covers the employees of the insured, either employed or engaged by him in a goods carriage.

It does not cover any other kind of employee and therefore, someone who travels not being an authorised agent in place of the owner of goods, and claims to be an employee of the owner of goods, cannot be covered by the statutory policy and to hold otherwise would tantamount to causing violence to the language employed in the Statute.
Therefore, we conclude that the insurer would not be liable to indemnify the insured."
Mr. Singh further submits that the insurance company has deposited the entire awarded sum with the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court Calcutta so necessary direction may be made.

sentences.text: 2 However, Mr. Singh further admits that by virtue of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Urmila Halder the fixed compensation of this case would be 5,00,000/-.
Learned advocate Mr. Saidur Rahaman, appearing on behalf of the claimants submits that the learned Tribunal has not committed any error by directing the insurance company to pay the compensation.
He submits that the fact goes to show that the present victim was the labour, who was engaged by M/s. Kalpataru Power Transmission Ltd. to load and unload the electric polls at the truck.
He submits that they are the representatives of the owner of the goods, so they are entitled to get the compensation.
Heard the learned advocates and perused the materials on record.
It appears that the present victim is one of the labour, who died due to the fatal accident by the truck carrying the electric polls.
The fact shows that the truck was hired by M/s. Kalpataru Power Transmission Ltd. from the owner to carry the polls.
It is true that the necessity of the labourers to load and unload of the electric polls can not denied, but they cannot be termed as an re[resemttoveof the owner of the electric polls.
Considering the situation of the present victim being labourers can be termed as 'gratuitous passenger'.

In Sanjeev Kumar Samrat (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that though the insurance company may not liable to pay compensation in terms of Section 147(1)(b)(i) of the MV Act, but in compliance to and the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Baljit Kaur and ors., the Insurance Company may be directed to pay the compensation and thereafter they are at liberty to recover the same to the owner of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Baljit Kaur and ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, it appears to be that the same principle be applicable.
However, in consideration to the observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurnce Co. Ltd. Vs.Urmila Halder, the fixed compensation would be Rs.5,00,000/-.

entities.text: New India Assurnce Co. Ltd. Vs.Urmila Halder
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that Insurance Company has deposited the entire award sum of Rs.4,25,500/-along with the statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/-.
The said amount must have carried some interest.
The Office of the learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta is directed to disburse the amount in the name of the claimant, according to the direction of the learned Tribunal within four weeks.

The rest amount of Rs. 50,000/- along with 6% per annum interest from the date of filing of the claim application is to be paid by the Insurance company directly to the claimants at their bank account to be furnished by them to the office of the Insurance Company within six weeks from the date of receiving the information along with bank particulars, directly to their bank account according to the proportion fixed by the learned Tribunal.

After such payment of insurance company is at liberty to recover the entire awarded sum from the owner of the offending vehicle according to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Baljit Kaur (supra).
The payment of compensation is subject to ascertainment of payment of deficit Court fees, if any.
The learned Tribunal shall act upon the certified copy of this order to receive the deficit Court fees, if any.
